5 ترنّح He inclined from side to side, by reason of intoxication &c; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ ارتنح , (K,) and ↓ رَنَّحَ [app. a mistranscription for رُنِّحَ]. (TA.) He inclined, and went round. (TA.) ―
-b2- (tropical:) It (a branch) inclined from side to side, being blown by the wind. (A.) ―
-b3- ترنّح بَيْنَ أَمْرَيْنِ (tropical:) He wavered between two things. (A.) ―
-b4- ترنّح عَلَى فُلَانٍ (tropical:) He was, or became, inimical to such a one, domineering, and exalting himself. (A.) ―
-b5- And ترنّح He sipped wine (شَرَاب) by little and little. (AHn, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
